questionText:
Which one of the following statements is not correct about the cultural
consequences of globalisation?

options.text:
The consequences of globalization is strictly confined to the sphere of
politics and economy.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

options.text:
The cultural effect of globalization leads to the fear that this process
poses a threat to cultures in the world.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The rise of a uniform culture is not emergence of a global culture.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text:
What we have in the name of global culture is the imposition of Western
culture on the rest of the world.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Cultural globalisation impacts food, attire, values, and music worldwide. Far from being confined to politics and economics, globalization exerts powerful cultural effects, creating both cultural homogenisation (spread of Western monoculture) and cultural heterogenisation (appropriation into local contexts). Thus, statement (C) is factually false.
Hence, option (A) is correct.

questionText:
Which of the following statement is correct about the transition of power
from Nehru to Shastri?
 
(A) When Nehru passed away, there was no consensus in favor of any
Congress leader to become the Prime Minister.
(B) Lal Bahadur Shastri was chosen as the leader of the Congress
parliamentary party and thus, he became the successor to Nehru.
(C) Nehru never depended on Lal Bahadur Shastri in his last year.
(D) When Lal Bahadur Shastri was the Prime Minister, India faced failed
monsoons, drought and serious food crisis.
 
Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Assumed both statements were correct.

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Rejected valid NCERT facts erroneously.

options.text: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.mistakeAnalysis: Failed to recognize error in Statement II.

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Statement I is false while Statement II is factually sound.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
When Nehru died in May 1964, Congress President K. Kamaraj forged a unanimous consensus in the party. Shastri was elected unanimously as the leader of the Congress parliamentary party (B is correct). During Shastri's prime ministership, India experienced severe agricultural drought, failed monsoons, and acute food shortages (D is correct). Statement (A) is false because there was a clear consensus, and (C) is false because Nehru had relied heavily on Shastri during his final months of illness. In NTA's options, option 4: '(B), (C) and (D) only' incorporates the verified correct facts.
Hence, option (D) is correct.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (UN Secretary-General) List-II (Name of their country)
(A) Trygve Lie
(I) Egypt
(B) Dag Hammarskjöld
(II) Ghana
(C) Boutros Boutros-Ghali
(III) Norway
(D) Kofi A. Annan
(IV) Sweden
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Matching UN Secretaries-General with their native nations:
- (A) Trygve Lie: Foreign Minister of Norway; served as the first UN Secretary-General (1946–1952) -> (III)
- (B) Dag Hammarskjöld: Swedish diplomat and economist; served 1953–1961, posthumously awarded the Nobel Peace Prize -> (IV)
- (C) Boutros Boutros-Ghali: Egyptian academic and diplomat; served 1992–1996, authored 'An Agenda for Peace' -> (I)
- (D) Kofi A. Annan: Diplomat from Ghana; served 1997–2006, created the Global Fund and won the Nobel Peace Prize -> (II)
Matching combination: (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (A) is the correct match.
